items.title: Dead crabs and a free port
items.dek: Jeanie Finlay's new documentary follows Teesside fishers demanding to know why the shellfish died. In Sight and Sound, Nick Bradshaw reads it as a film about who gets believed in a region long left to fend for itself.
paragraphs: Since 2021, the coast of north-east England has been the scene of a grim recurring spectacle: crabs and lobsters dying in their thousands around the Tees estuary, their bodies washing up on beaches as far south as Scarborough. For the people who fish those waters, the die-offs have meant collapsing catches. For the documentary-maker Jeanie Finlay, who was born in Stockton-on-Tees, they became the occasion to return home with a camera for the first time since Sound It Out, her 2011 portrait of Teesside's last record shop.

The result, All Rivers Spill Their Stories to the Sea, made together with the fisherman Stan Rennie, opened in UK cinemas on 23 October. Rennie is its hinge. Unwilling to accept the official shrug, he set up the North East Fishing Collective and gathered some sixty fellow fishers behind a single demand: an honest account of what happened, and action to match it. Finlay follows him on the boat, in the pub and in the community hall, and onwards to testimony before a parliamentary committee.

The questions the film raises are concrete. Local scientists suspect that contaminants buried in the silt of old industrial sites were stirred up, and the obvious candidate for the stirring is the dredging of the harbour for Teesworks, the vast free port development championed by the Tees Valley mayor, Ben Houchen. Houchen appears in media clips denying any link, and, according to BBC reporting cited in the review, an official report backed him up. The scientists interviewed reject that conclusion; the film gives their dissent the hearing it was denied elsewhere.

Reviewing it for Sight and Sound, Nick Bradshaw is clear about where the film's sympathies lie, and about why they matter. In his reading, the dead shellfish are only the newest chapter in a longer story of a region gutted by the deindustrialisation of the 1970s and 1980s and then courted, in the Brexit years, with promises of regeneration. One of the film's most telling moments, he notes, shows Thérèse Coffey, then environment secretary, at the Commons dispatch box, rebuking an MP for questioning her department's scientists. Expertise, in that scene, functions less as a method of finding out than as a wall.

What makes the film more than an exposé is its refusal to manufacture a verdict it cannot prove. Bradshaw acknowledges that the investigation runs into closed doors and unanswered questions, but he treats that frustration as part of the subject rather than a flaw: the opacity is the story. The solidarity on screen, fishers who were never activists learning to speak to ministers, is where the film locates its hope.

It is worth separating the record from the reading. That the die-offs occurred, that the free port was built, and that the official explanation is contested are matters of fact; that they add up to a parable of patronage and abandonment is the critic's argument, and a persuasive one. Only by watching who is permitted to define a disaster, the film suggests, can a community begin to contest it.

glossary.en: a sudden mass death of animals or plants in one area
the central element on which something depends
an authority's dismissive refusal to take a problem seriously
to disturb something so that it rises or spreads; also, to provoke
the lectern in the House of Commons from which ministers speak
stripped of its core economy or contents
to try to win someone's support by offering inducements
the quality of being hard to see into or understand; lack of transparency
a story used to illustrate a moral or political lesson

items.grammar: The last sentence uses subject–auxiliary inversion after a fronted 'only' phrase: 'Only by watching who is permitted to define a disaster … can a community begin to contest it.' When 'only' + an adverbial (only by, only then, only after) opens the clause, the auxiliary comes before the subject, as in a question. The structure is formal and emphatic, stressing that this condition is the one and only route to the result.
items.grammar_zh: 最后一句在句首用了 only 引导的状语，因此主句发生部分倒装：Only by watching … can a community begin to contest it。only + 状语（only by / only then / only after）放在句首时，助动词要提到主语前面，语序像疑问句。这种结构语气正式而强调，突出“唯有这一条件”才能带来结果。
questions: Why does the film's refusal to deliver a definitive verdict strengthen rather than weaken its political argument, according to the review?
How does the piece distinguish the established facts of the Tees die-offs from the critic's interpretation of them?
What does the scene at the dispatch box suggest about the relationship between official expertise and local knowledge?

sources.title: Nick Bradshaw, review of All Rivers Spill Their Stories to the Sea, Sight and Sound (BFI), 15 October 2026

items.title: Mia's Diary 3: A dog, the rain and a seagull
paragraphs: Monday, 16 November 2026. I had a lovely weekend, so I want to write about it.
On Saturday morning I was cleaning my flat when someone knocked on the door. It was Mr Patel, my neighbour. He was holding a small brown dog. “This is Biscuit,” he said. “He wants to meet you!”
Biscuit jumped on my legs and I laughed. Mr Patel is a teacher from Leicester. He asked me to walk with them in the park in the afternoon.
We walked for an hour. While we were walking, it started to rain, so we ran into a small café. Biscuit was very wet, and he shook water all over a man's newspaper!

On Sunday I met Sam at the harbour. We were sitting by the water when a seagull took his sandwich. Sam was talking about a book on ships, and he didn't see it. I laughed so much that I nearly fell off the bench.
Now it's evening and I'm tired. I like Bristol. My neighbour is kind, my friend is funny, and the seagulls are very fast!
paragraphs_zh: 2026年11月16日，星期一。我度过了一个愉快的周末，所以想把它写下来。
星期六早上，我正在打扫公寓，这时有人敲门。是我的邻居帕特尔先生。他抱着一只棕色的小狗。“这是饼干，”他说，“它想认识你！”
饼干跳到我的腿上，我笑了。帕特尔先生是来自莱斯特的老师。他邀请我下午和他们一起去公园散步。
我们走了一个小时。散步的时候开始下雨，于是我们跑进一家小咖啡馆。饼干浑身湿透，还把水甩得一位男士的报纸上到处都是！
星期天我在港口和萨姆见面。我们正坐在水边，一只海鸥抢走了他的三明治。萨姆正在讲一本关于船的书，没有看到它。我笑得差点从长椅上掉下来。
现在是晚上，我很累。我喜欢布里斯托。我的邻居很善良，我的朋友很有趣，而海鸥跑得飞快！

glossary.en: to hit a door with your hand to ask to come in
a person who lives near you
to go up into the air and land on something
to move quickly up and down or side to side
in every part of a place or thing
a place by the sea where boats stay
a white sea bird that is often near the coast

items.grammar: We use the past simple for finished actions: “Biscuit jumped on my legs.” We use the past continuous (was/were + -ing) for an action in progress when something else happened: “I was cleaning my flat when someone knocked on the door.” Use when for the short action and while for the long one.
items.grammar_zh: 一般过去时表示已经完成的动作：“Biscuit jumped on my legs.”过去进行时（was/were + 动词-ing）表示某个时刻正在进行的动作，常和另一个突然发生的动作搭配：“I was cleaning my flat when someone knocked on the door.”短动作用 when，长动作用 while。中文常用“正在……的时候”，英语要靠时态来表达。
questions: What was Mia doing when Mr Patel knocked on the door?
And you? What were you doing at this time yesterday?
